chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from others from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yasin al-Darir from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about the boundary of circumambulation around the House, such that if one exits it, they are not considered to have circumambulated the House. He said: 'The people, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), used to circumambulate the House and the Maqam (Station), whereas you today circumambulate between the Maqam and the House. Therefore, the boundary is from the place of the Maqam today; whoever passes it is not a circumambulator. The boundary before today and the boundary today are one: the extent of the space between the Maqam and the House. And from all sides of the House, whoever circumambulates and moves away from its sides by more than that extent, has circumambulated the non-House, in the manner of one who circumambulates the Mosque, because they have circumambulated outside the boundary and their circumambulation is invalid.' And it is appropriate for one who circumambulates to walk with a pace between brisk walking and strolling, neither hurrying nor moving slowly. He narrated that.

key_terms.بَيْنَ الْمَقَامِ وَ بَيْنَ الْبَيْتِ: Between the Maqam and the House

ai.seo_question: What is the boundary of Tawaf around the Kaaba and how does the position of the Maqam affect its validity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential boundary (hadd) for the validity of Tawaf, noting that while the Maqam Ibrahim was originally within the circumambulation area during the Prophet's time, it was later moved outside, establishing the current space between the Maqam and the Kaaba as the limit. It further prescribes a moderate walking pace (not too fast, not too slow) to ensure reverence and correctness in the ritual. This ruling highlights the dynamic nature of fiqh in adapting to physical changes in the Holy Mosque while maintaining the spiritual essence of the act.
